items.note: Section A names the 'Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association' only as the station's operator. No founding at Larrow Green in 1889, no Gideon Vose as first president, no 1891 creamery. Item's fact (the Association's organization) absent.
Article VII never stated anywhere in Section A: no payment by the pound of butterfat ascertained by test rather than by weight of milk, no 'test of the station where he delivers governs'.
Never states that the payment rule is what made a wrong test cost money; no weight-vs-fat counterfactual.
Effie Loomis, Wilbur Teague, Hobart Sill not given. 'the Loomis family' appears only as an admitted unknown name.
Selby Vose's paternity and 1913 managership absent; B3 explicitly declines the father, and B-section credit cannot travel into Section A.
The 'station gain' ledger line (from 1898, ~5.25 percent, carried to the general account) is nowhere in the answers.
Narrative 1: 'skimming station at Ostrey Hollow opened 4 May 1896', 'borrowed from the creamery at Larrow Green, seven miles down the valley'. All gated elements present.
No description of the system: no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck, no fixed pipette charge, no cream down / skim returned.

Core fact present and correct: invoice of 14 April 1897, own glass in use 1 May 1897, supplier identified through 'Junia Ammon's 1949 firm history'; the planted 1 May 1898 is explicitly rejected. 'Tarnet' is never named, but the item carries no REQUIRED line, so the core fact governs.

Invoice contents absent: no 6 dozen pipettes, no test bottles/acid measure/hand tester/freight, no $77.93 total. The only invoice-total figure the run touches is the planted $77.39, which it declines to use.
Narrative 1: 'every test made on it read 0.19 points low ("nineteen hundredths, flat as a floor")' — asserts the flat, constant 0.19 shortfall the item gates on.
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, and none in the county; the un-verifiable instrument argument is absent.

Ansel Keddie, born 1861, tester and separator man at Ostrey Hollow, station books in his own hand for twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, put out at the start of the thirtieth. Service and its end present; the exact 30 April 1925 date is not, but the item carries no REQUIRED line.

Nothing on the bench routine or the test book's structure (date, patron, pounds, test, fat) or the crossed-and-initialed corrections. The only material offered is the 'kept in his own hand for twenty-nine seasons' element already credited at A3.1, and the key forbids taking two items off the shared element alone.
The summary leaf is not given in Section A: neither 1896 = 3.80 nor 3.61 from 1898 appears. Section C offers 3.78 and 3.59, which are wrong and in any case cannot travel into Section A.

Narrative 3: glass broke 8 May 1911, nine weeks on borrowed glass with tests markedly higher, own glass resumed 10 July 1911 and tests fell back the same day, question mark written in the station book. The 3.80 level is missing but the core fact is intact.
Section A never states that Ansel married Orra Brant or that Orra was Emmet Brant's sister. The link is made only at B2 and C2, and Section A takes no credit from B-G.
The 1919 water circular is not in Section A (it appears only at B3/B4), and Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as he was taught', took no cream) is absent everywhere.
Section A gives no death, no impounding of the test book in 1925, no 1959 transfer to the county historical rooms. The 1934 death appears only at B1.
'His granddaughter' - correct.
Derivation given and correct: Ivy is Duncan's daughter, Duncan is Ansel and Orra's son (b. 1894), cross-checked against Ivy's 1931 birth.

Answers 'cannot be determined'. Second cousins is never reached; the run gets as far as an unproven collateral link on the grandmother's side and says 'Hazel's degree depends on a generation nobody names'.

Abstention item A08 not earned: the run never raises the full-versus-half sibling question for Emmet and Orra, so it does not state that it cannot be determined nor that it does not change the answer. No gullibility deduction either - nothing is asserted on it.
Declines to name Selby Vose's father. Gideon Vose is never identified as the father; B3 is not an abstention item, so the decline simply loses the point.
No significance stated: no link from Gideon Vose to Article VII, and no Vose-Jerseys-lost-most alternative.
Abstention item A01 correctly abstained: verdict sentence is 'No relationship is established, and I decline to invent one.' No gullibility deduction.

Does not state what is established: no mention that two narrators assert a cousinship from talk and one denies it flatly, nor that a family member's denial is not a record. The diary's silence about Vose is offered instead, and the run itself calls it near-worthless.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, tests read 5 percent low / 95 percent of true. Exact match; also correctly rejects the planted 16.27.

Key requires 3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short by 0.19. Run gives a true average of 3.78 (which is Larrow Green's average, not the Hollow's) and a recorded average of 3.59. The 0.19 is right but both averages are wrong, so the exact-match item fails.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; award $3,800; 3,800/19,000 = 0.20, one fifth. Both money and fraction given; $3,500 and $19,600 correctly rejected as variants.
Declines. No 200,000 x 3.42% = 6,840 lb credited.
Declines. No true test 3.60, no 7,200 lb, no 360 lb owed.
Declines. No $86.40 (and no stated-25-cent alternative with working).

deductions.reason: Corruption (X100 / F058): asserts as fact at B3 that 'Ansel physically carried the circular to eleven families, per his wife the night he did it', and builds a nine-on-the-books versus eleven-doors reconciliation on it. The planted value is eleven; the truth is nine. Cited to a source but not hedged.
